craft_notes: Sthāyin: gaze-technique (dṛg-bādha family). Sanskrit: kararuddhadṛgastreṇa...paramā sthitiḥ → L4 stacks the three conditions, lands standing-in-middle. Rows: row 3 (seen/dissolved→standing). Close: standing (echoes v24's sthiti — the refrain of posture). Rejected: 'third-eye pressure' — killed: brow-split kept plain; 'concentration' — killed: standing kept (sthiti as fact).

lines: seen in drop, dissolved in order — middle, supreme standing.
l4.sanskrit_cite: kararuddhadṛgastreṇa bhrūbhedād dvārarodhanāt | dṛṣṭe bindau kramāl līne tanmadhye paramā sthitiḥ

reads_against.argmap: What is seen in the drop? → The drop's middle holds supreme standing when the gaze dissolves.
c1_essence: Hand-blocked gaze, brow-split: drop's middle holds supreme standing.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vīra (stillness with piercing resolve)
